slice: App map grids transcribed from published screenshots

records.topic: tester Power Tuner map 'Exciting Connect' (full grid)
records.statement: A tester's 'Exciting Connect' Power Tuner map for the 2023 YZ450F leans fuel 1-2 steps at low and high throttle (adds 1 at 40% throttle from 5,000 rpm up) and retards ignition 1-3 degrees everywhere, most at low rpm and small throttle openings.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested app screenshot (2023 YZ450F media bike)

records.notes: Transcribed exactly from the published Power Tuner app screenshot. Values are offsets from the stock map (fuel steps, ignition degrees). Same engine generation runs 2023-2026; confirm the app accepts it for later years.

records.topic: tester Power Tuner map 'Control Torque' (full grid)
records.statement: A tester's 'Control Torque' Power Tuner map for the 2023 YZ450F adds 1 step of fuel almost everywhere and advances ignition 1-3 degrees below 10,000 rpm, leaving the top-rpm column at stock.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested app screenshot (2023 YZ450F media bike)

records.notes: Transcribed exactly from the published Power Tuner app screenshot; offsets from stock.

records.topic: 'Top End/Rev' Power Tuner map (full grid, custom breakpoints)
records.statement: A 'Top End/Rev' Power Tuner map for the 2023 YZ250F, said to come from Yamaha's own R&D team, leans fuel 1-3 steps up to 11,500 rpm and adds 1 at 12,000 rpm, with 1-3 degrees more ignition in the mid-range, to pull harder through second, third and fourth gear.

values.fuel_grid: rows = throttle 5/15/60/80 %, columns = 4,500/9,500/11,500/12,000 rpm (breakpoints moved from default)

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested, 2023 YZ250F optional Power Tuner maps

records.notes: Published by a tester, who attributes the map to Yamaha's R&D team; kept at TUNER tier because Yamaha has not published it. The grid uses custom breakpoints, which the app allows.

records.topic: tester Power Tuner map 'Free Feeling' (full grid)
records.statement: A tester's 'Free Feeling' Power Tuner map for the 2019-2023 YZ250F leans fuel 1-3 steps across the grid and advances ignition 1-3 degrees (retards 2 at 12,000 rpm and 20% throttle), for free-revving top-end power and less engine braking.

values.purpose: free-revving high-rpm power; less engine braking

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested, 2023 YZ250F optional Power Tuner maps

records.notes: Transcribed exactly from the app screenshot (saved July 2019). The article recommends it for the 2023 YZ250F; same engine generation 2019-2023.

records.topic: tester Rideology map for the 2027 KX250 (full grid)
records.statement: A tester's optional Rideology map for the 2027 KX250 adds 1 step of fuel at 40-80% throttle and takes 2 away at 10-30%, and adds 3 degrees of ignition everywhere below 4,000 rpm and at 10-30% throttle across the rev range.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested, 2027 KX250 optional ECU map

records.notes: Transcribed exactly from the Rideology app screenshots (FI and IG pages). Effect reported: a little more pull out of corners and a longer second-gear pull.

records.statement: The Rideology app's KX tuning grid is 6 x 6: throttle 10, 20, 30, 40, 60 and 80% against 2,500, 3,000, 4,000, 6,000, 8,000 and 10,000 rpm, with separate fuel (FI) and ignition (IG) pages.

source.name: Rideology app screenshot published with a 2027 KX250 map

records.notes: Axes read from a 2027 KX250 screenshot; assumed the same on 2025-2026 KX250 in the same app. Check on the bike.

records.topic: calibration-kit fuel map saved as 'Aggr Riding 3' (fuel grid)
records.statement: A KX FI Calibration Kit fuel map saved as 'Aggr Riding 3', published with a 2021 KX450 test, leaves 2,000 rpm and 10-degree throttle at stock and adds 2-4 steps of fuel from 3,000 rpm up, most (4) at 30-40 degrees throttle.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested, 2021-2022 KX450 map photo

records.notes: Only the fuel page was published; ignition not shown. Units are calibration-kit steps.
